name: Full Table Scan - Large Dataset

context.description: Query retrieves entire policy table with no WHERE clause

root_causes: No WHERE clause filtering
No index on common filter columns
Full sequential scan required
suggested_optimizations: Add WHERE clause to filter by status='ACTIVE'
Create index on 'status' column
Use LIMIT clause if pagination is possible
Consider materialized view for common queries

name: JSON Field Filtering Without Index

context.description: Filtering on JSON field without index - slow for high frequency

root_causes: JSON_EXTRACT cannot use traditional indexes
High query frequency amplifies overhead
Entire table scan required for JSON comparison
suggested_optimizations: Create generated column: state_gen AS JSON_EXTRACT(data, '$.policy.state')
Index the generated column
Denormalize: store state in separate column
Use JSON_TABLE for better optimization

name: Complex Join With JSON Processing
query: SELECT p.policy_id, p.premium_amount, c.claim_count FROM policy_data p LEFT JOIN (SELECT policy_id, COUNT(*) as claim_count FROM claims_data GROUP BY policy_id) c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(p.data, '$.policy.state') IN ('CA', 'TX')

context.description: Multiple joins with aggregation and JSON filtering

root_causes: Subquery in JOIN clause forces full scan of claims table
GROUP BY on large table is expensive
JSON filter applied after joins instead of before
suggested_optimizations: Pre-aggregate claims data in materialized view
Apply JSON filter before JOIN (move to WHERE)
Create index on claims_data.policy_id
Use window function instead of subquery: DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id)

name: High Frequency Query - Low Latency

context.description: Fast query but called 50,000 times per hour = 100K ms total/hour overhead

root_causes: Low individual latency (2ms) but massive cumulative impact
35% cache misses causing repeated DB hits
No application-level caching
suggested_optimizations: Implement Redis caching layer (99% cache hit target)
Use connection pooling to reduce overhead
Cache entire config table in application memory
Set cache TTL: 5-10 minutes for config table

name: Nested Subquery - Multiple Levels
query: SELECT * FROM policies WHERE premium_amount > (SELECT AVG(premium_amount) FROM policies WHERE state = (SELECT state FROM top_selling_states LIMIT 1))

context.subquery_repetition: subqueries run for each outer row
context.description: Correlated subqueries evaluated per outer row

root_causes: Nested subqueries evaluated multiple times
Correlated subquery pattern is inefficient
No query plan optimization by optimizer
suggested_optimizations: Use EXPLAIN PLAN to verify optimizer behavior
Rewrite with JOIN: avoid nested subqueries
Use CTE (WITH clause): define intermediate results once
Example: WITH top_state AS (...), avg_premium AS (...) SELECT ...

name: Aggregation with Multiple Joins
query: SELECT p.state, COUNT(*) as policy_count, SUM(p.premium_amount) as total_premium, AVG(c.claim_amount) as avg_claim FROM policy_data p LEFT JOIN claims_data c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id GROUP BY p.state HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
root_causes: JOIN creates Cartesian product before grouping
Each policy can have multiple claims, multiplying rows
Heavy aggregation on large result set
suggested_optimizations: Pre-aggregate claims by policy: GROUP BY before JOIN
Use ONLY necessary columns in SELECT
Add index on (policy_id, claim_amount) for claims table
Materialize intermediate aggregations if repeated daily

name: Logging Table Scan - Time Range Query
query: SELECT * FROM application_logs WHERE timestamp BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-01-31' AND log_level IN ('ERROR', 'CRITICAL')

context.description: Large logging table scan with multiple filters

root_causes: Table has 500M+ rows, no partitioning by date
Index on timestamp exists but combined with IN clause
No index on log_level column
suggested_optimizations: Partition table by DATE/MONTH on timestamp column
Create composite index: (timestamp, log_level)
Archive old logs to separate table/storage
Use UNION with separate indexes: (timestamp ASC, level=ERROR UNION level=CRITICAL)

name: Anomaly: Latency Spike
query: SELECT * FROM transaction_ledger WHERE account_id = ? AND created_date > DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)

context.description: 10x latency increase during specific time window

root_causes: Table lock acquired by long-running BACKUP operation
Memory pressure: database buffer pool evicted
Index statistics outdated: query plan reverted to slow execution
Disk I/O spike: concurrent maintenance jobs
suggested_optimizations: Schedule BACKUP outside business hours
Implement query timeout (e.g., 10 second max)
Set up automated ANALYZE TABLE on schedule
Monitor: CPU, memory, disk I/O in correlation with latency
Add instance-level metrics: buffer pool hit ratio, active connections

name: UPDATE with JOIN - Row Lock Contention
query: UPDATE policies p JOIN claims c ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id SET p.status = 'CLOSED' WHERE c.resolved_date < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)

context.description: Batch update with join causing lock contention

root_causes: UPDATE acquires locks on 50K rows
Concurrent transactions waiting for those row locks
No batching: updates 50K rows in single transaction
suggested_optimizations: Batch updates: process 1000 rows per transaction with COMMIT between batches
Add index on (resolved_date, policy_id) for faster JOIN
Use low_priority UPDATE to reduce blocking priority
Consider triggers or async job queue instead of synchronous update

name: Knowledge Base Query - Configuration Driven System
query: SELECT rule_id, condition_json, action_json FROM policy_rules WHERE product_type = ? AND region = ? AND status = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY priority DESC LIMIT 50
root_causes: Index exists but 5000 QPS still stresses connection pool
No caching: rules are static, same result returned
Database connection overhead dominates
suggested_optimizations: Implement Redis cache: KEY = {product_type}:{region}:{status}
Load entire rules table into application memory at startup (100KB)
Use connection pooling with min_connections=20, max_connections=50
Set cache invalidation on rule table INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers
